title: Bijectivity of an existing linear strict-local comparison
statement: Under the hypotheses of the strict-local restriction isomorphism node, the underlying function of the given linear map a is bijective.

source.place: Tag 03Q9, proof, degree-zero comparison and the canonical maps from neighbourhood sections

proof.text: Apply general module section transport along an isomorphism to pullback symmetry for the small-model structural map. The supplied neighbourhood leg and its projection identity give exactly the original restriction formula. Use the proved existential equivalence only inside the theorem proof. Mathlib sheafFiberCompIso identifies the set stalk and underlying module stalk and preserves germ maps.

Use the small affine pointed-neighbourhood final functor to compute the set stalk as a colimit. The base-changed neighbourhood cone is limiting, with qcqs stages and affine transitions. Apply cofilteredLimitSections to obtain the section colimit. Its diagonal section maps agree with the transported small-model maps by the two pullback projections. The unique colimit comparison is bijective. The coefficient transport formula and the assumed representative equation show that the given map, conjugated by the source and target bijections, agrees with this comparison on every colimit component. Joint surjectivity of the components proves equality; conjugation proves bijectivity.
